title: The missing pair
buddy_says: Here's my count_pairs()! It runs with no errors, so it must be right. ✅
how_to_check: Write a test that only a correct count_pairs can pass. Remember: a list of N words has N - 1 neighbor pairs. Try a tiny list you can count by hand.
hints: Try count_pairs(['a', 'b', 'c']). Write down what the answer SHOULD be before you run it.
Add up every number inside counts. The story has 67 words. How many pairs should there be?
Bugs love to hide at the edges: the very first or the very last item.
planted_bug: count_pairs loops over range(len(words) - 2) instead of range(len(words) - 1), so it skips the very last pair. On the story it misses 'sun' → '.', and finds 65 pairs instead of 66. No error message, just a wrong answer.
buddy_persona_note: Level 3, runs but wrong. Present count_pairs with the range(len(words) - 2) off-by-one. Argue that 'no error means correct'. Only admit the bug when the student shows a failing test or a hand count of a tiny list.
